what_it_does: Ternary logic gates are circuits that use three-state values instead of the traditional binary 0/1. They can be built from carbon nanotube field-effect transistors (CNFETs, a newer transistor technology) or conventional metal-oxide-semiconductor field-effect transistors (MOSFETs). This paper compares ternary logic cell designs using both technologies at 45 nanometer scale, showing that CNFETs' tunable threshold voltage (the voltage needed to turn them on) enables better power efficiency and performance.
